title: ‘I’m going for a few pints now’: nerves and joy as students collect their A-level results

paragraphs.en: There are few days that teenagers dread more than A-level results day , where students learn how the last two years of their lives will shape their futures, communicated through a few letters in an envelope.
The tension of walking into college to learn your fate is enough to keep most people awake the night before. For Hayden Bettson-Day, 18, the best solution was get it over with as early as possible.
“I was refreshing the Ucas page at 8 o’clock in the morning, waiting for it to go on,” Hayden said. “So, it was a definite bit of tension. My mum kept asking: ‘What is it? What did you get?”
What Hayden got was an A* in maths coupled with two As in chemistry and biology, which is enough to be accepted into Newcastle University to study medicine.
The 18-year-old is one of 450 students at Trinity sixth form academy, located in the town’s centre and part of the Trinity multi-academy trust, which has colleges throughout Yorkshire.
Aidan Chiu and Fran Whitehead, two of Hayden’s classmates, spoke about their own relief at their results, having both received A*s in chemistry.
“My mum’s on the phone to Bristol University,” said Aidan, who plans to study maths. “I have the grades I need, but she’s still calling them to make sure I got in. I can’t believe it.”

Fran, who will now study geology at the University of Exeter, said that the last two years had been difficult, but praised the college for helping her settle and supporting her as she readjusted to a new environment during such a pivotal time in her life.
